name: Mango Markets
tldr: The attacker pumped the price of a thinly traded token, used the inflated position as collateral, and borrowed everything else in the protocol.
what: Mango Markets was a trading and lending protocol on Solana that let users borrow against their positions.
happened: Using two accounts, the attacker pushed up the price of MNGO, Mango's own thin token, then borrowed real assets against the now "valuable" position.
bug: The protocol trusted a price that a single well-funded trader could move, and let that price back big loans.
prevent: Robust, manipulation-resistant oracles and strict limits on collateral from illiquid tokens.
lesson: A price is only as safe as the market behind it. The person behind it was later arrested; "it's just a trading strategy" did not hold up.
